plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Add to QQQI to increase income-focused holdings.
Trim CRWD to 10% to further reduce single-name concentration.
Hold remaining cash for safety and potential opportunities.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration risk, holding a larger cash buffer for stability. Drawdowns are expected to be minimal.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 3% and 2% respectively.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Buy SPXS at 4% to add a hedging element.
Slightly trim QQQI to 10% to rebalance towards broader diversification.
Maintain a balanced approach between growth and risk management.
balanced.read: This plan aims for risk-first growth with a target of approximately 2.5% monthly return. It balances broad index exposure with some leveraged ETFs and hedging, while reducing concentration. Drawdowns are managed but can be more significant than conservative.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Buy SPXS at 6% to add significant hedging.
Maintain CRWD at 14% as a strong performer.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to underperforming semiconductors.
Focus on high-conviction, high-scoring setups with wider stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets substantial growth, aiming for around 4% monthly return, but carries significantly higher risk. It leverages up on ETFs and concentrates in top setups, accepting larger potential drawdowns and the impact of ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad market exposure.
Sell CRWD and SMH to remove high-beta and volatile sector risk.
Focus on steady monthly distributions from income-oriented assets.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets approximately 1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing low drawdown. It shifts heavily into income-generating assets like QQQI and reduces exposure to growth and volatile sectors. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
